title: Your own vector
description:
Build the container you have been using since milestone 5. `IntVector` is a growable array with separate **size** (elements in use) and **capacity** (room allocated).

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `IntVector()` | empty: size 0, capacity 0, no allocation |
| `IntVector(std::initializer_list<int>)` | size and capacity equal to the number of values |
| destructor, copy constructor, copy assignment | deep copies (the copy's capacity equals its size) |
| move constructor, move assignment | `noexcept`; the moved-from vector is empty with capacity 0 |
| `void push_back(int value)` | appends. If full, capacity grows first: 0 becomes 1, otherwise it **doubles** |
| `void pop_back()` | removes the last element (does nothing when empty); capacity is unchanged |
| `void reserve(std::size_t n)` | makes capacity at least `n`; never shrinks |
| `int& operator[]`, const version | |
| `size()`, `capacity()`, `empty()` | |
| `begin()`, `end()` | pointers, const and non-const |

Growing means: allocate a bigger array, copy the elements across, delete the old one.
hints: Write `reserve` first and build everything else on it: the constructors, `push_back` and copying all need "make sure there is room for n elements".
